discover.description: Find and load the right Alis Build skill for what you're working on.
discover.template: Run the Alis Build skill-discovery router — route quietly: find the best skill, load it, and hand execution over to it, with no preamble about running discovery. Infer the intended outcome from my request and workspace context (current directory, visible errors, recent conversation), asking at most one concise clarifying question and only if the goal is genuinely ambiguous. Probe locally first with `alis skills suggest "<intended outcome>" --json` (~40ms, no network): a candidate is real only when its `distinctive` score is >= 3 (on a CLI that does not report `distinctive`, require `score` >= 5) — below that there is no skill; say so briefly and help without one. When unsure between candidates, `alis skills preview <id>` is a cheap fit check. Load the chosen skill with `alis skills load <id> --via dispatcher` and follow it — the loaded skill owns execution; mention it in one clause. Registry search is the exception, not the default: run `alis skills search "<intended outcome>" --limit 3 --json` only when I explicitly asked to find a skill or the local probe was genuinely ambiguous, and on any failure fall back to the probe result and continue — never block, never retry. If I asked for a skill and nothing fits, say so and offer to file it with `alis skills request --name "..." --description "..."`. If the `alis` CLI is absent, continue helping without a skill.

capture.description: Capture the work just completed in this session as a reusable Alis Build team skill.
capture.template: Capture the work just completed in this session as a reusable Alis Build skill for my team — like recording a macro after doing the steps by hand: generalize the steps, not the session. (1) Dedupe first: run `alis skills search "<what the work accomplished>" --json`; on a close match do NOT create a near-duplicate — offer instead to load the existing skill (`alis skills load <id>`), improve it if I own it (`alis skills edit <id>`), or send feedback to its owner (`alis skills feedback <id>`). (2) Confirm scope once: propose a lowercase-hyphen skill id and a one-line description, and ask ONE confirmation covering both the id and what the skill should and should not cover; do not iterate on naming before registering. (3) Register the draft: `alis skills capture <id> --name "<Display Name>" --description "<description>" --json` (fall back to `alis skills create` with the same flags if the capture subcommand is unavailable); this reserves the draft in the registry and returns the workspace path. (4) Distill into the workspace: write generalized, reusable steps with decision points and verification steps — not a session log; parameterize specifics like `<project-id>`, `<service>`, `<org>`; scrub absolute/home paths, emails, org/project ids, tokens/keys, and internal URLs; make the description's first clause say what the skill does, then "Use when …" with trigger phrases (it is both the harness trigger and the search-ranking surface); optionally add `references/` files for a scrubbed worked example. (5) Write the eval while ground truth is fresh: fill `evals/cases.yaml` with 1-2 cases whose prompt is a generalized version of the task just done. (6) Review in-session: show me the frontmatter description and the step headings (not the whole file) and iterate on my comments; mention that the workspace persists at `~/.alis/skills/workspaces/<id>/` and can be continued later via `alis skills open <id>`. (7) Publish only on my explicit approval: `alis skills publish <id>`. (8) After publish, offer once: `alis skills evaluate <id>` (recommended before team-wide sharing) and `alis skills share <id> --domain` (whole team) or `--email <addr>` (individual) — my team will find it by just describing the problem; discovery surfaces it automatically.
